scenes.tts: After a hard sprint, your legs may burn. Bread dough puffs up with bubbles. In summer, parts of the deep Chesapeake Bay hold very little oxygen. All three are about one question. How does the energy in food become energy a cell can use, with or without oxygen?
scenes.visual: Three cards (sprint, dough, Bay) appear; they shrink away and the essential question fills the frame.

scenes.tts: Cells break down glucose, a sugar, in a process called cellular respiration. The first steps happen in the cytoplasm. Most of the A T P is made in the mitochondria, which are organelles in plant, animal and fungal cells. With oxygen, glucose becomes carbon dioxide and water. Much of the released energy is captured in a small molecule called A T P.
scenes.visual: A cell outline: glucose chip enters the cytoplasm; a mitochondrion appears; oxygen goes in; carbon dioxide and water come out; an ATP chip leaves.

scenes.tts: A T P is a molecule with three phosphate groups in a row. A phosphate group is a cluster of atoms that can be added or removed. When A T P reacts with water, the end phosphate group comes off. What is left is A D P, with two phosphate groups. The reaction releases energy that the cell uses for work. A T P is not energy. It is a molecule that carries energy.
scenes.visual: ATP as a labelled block with three P squares; a water chip arrives; the end P detaches; the block becomes ADP; an energy arrow goes to cell work.

scenes.tts: Putting a phosphate group back onto A D P takes energy. Cellular respiration supplies that energy. So A T P and A D P go round in a cycle. Cell work turns A T P into A D P. Respiration turns A D P back into A T P. A cell keeps only a small supply of A T P, so it rebuilds it all the time.
scenes.visual: A two-arrow loop between ATP and ADP plus phosphate; a dot circulates; a small stack shows the small supply.
scenes.narration: Putting a phosphate group back onto ADP takes energy. Cellular respiration supplies that energy. So ATP and ADP go round in a cycle. Cell work turns ATP into ADP. Respiration turns ADP back into ATP. A cell keeps only a small supply of ATP, so it rebuilds it all the time.

scenes.tts: Aerobic means using oxygen. Anaerobic means without oxygen. Without oxygen, muscle cells and yeast use fermentation. It makes a small amount of A T P from glucose. The S O L calls this anaerobic respiration. In muscle, fermentation makes lactate. In yeast, it makes ethanol and carbon dioxide. The carbon dioxide forms the bubbles that make dough rise.

scenes.tts: With oxygen, one glucose gives about thirty to thirty-two A T P. Fermentation gives only two. But by one 2024 estimate, fermentation makes A T P faster for the same amount of enzyme, in yeast and mammal cells. In a sprint, muscles use A T P faster than aerobic respiration alone can rebuild it. So fermentation adds A T P. Food energy reaches cell work through A T P, rebuilt with oxygen or without it.
